neighbours.label: a preposition ('by', 'during') introducing a weather or natural force as the cause or setting of an event (by the wind, during the storm), as against the same prepositions introducing people or ordinary events
fire: Several fences were knocked down by the wind on Saturday night.
The old pier was badly damaged by the waves last winter.
Many schools closed during the blizzard in early February.
The hillside path was washed away by heavy rain in April.
Two fishing boats sank during the typhoon off the coast.
The tents were flattened by a sudden gust before dawn.
Power lines came down during the ice storm last week.
The farmhouse roof was ripped off by a tornado in May.
quiet: Several fences were painted white by the neighbors on Saturday.
The old pier was rebuilt by a local company last winter.
Many schools closed during the teachers' strike in early February.
The hillside path was cleared by volunteers in April.
Two fishing boats were sold during the auction in the harbor.
The tents were set up by the scouts before dawn.
Power lines were repaired during the holiday last week.
The farmhouse roof was replaced by a builder in May.

predictions: fire 0.35-0.75 on ' by' or ' during' before wind, waves, rain, storms, floods; 'by' before a person and 'during' before a meeting or meal below 0.25
notes: Card: ' by' x7 (picked up by the wind, ripped apart by tides, cut off by the tide), ' during' (wet weather), ' following' (rain event); the + pole suppresses strong/heavy/intense. Probe: during the storm 0.731, torn off by the wind 0.573, destroyed by heavy rain 0.496, swamped by waves 0.477; written by her grandmother 0.018, during the lunch break 0.222. 'cut off by the army' also scored 0.356, so near misses avoid 'cut off'.
